source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ ወልድየ፡ ኵሎ፡ አርአይኩከ፡ ወ*ተፈጸመት፡ *ሥርዓተ፡ ኵሉ፡ ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማያት።

translation.text: “Now, my son, I have shown you everything, and the order of all the stars of the heavens has been completed.”

source.text: ወአርአየኒ፡ ኵሎ፡ ሥርዓቶሙ፡ *ለእሉ፡ እንተ፡ በኵሉ፡ ዕለት፡ ወበኵሉ፡ ዘመን፡ ዘበሥልጣን፡ ወበኵሉ፡ ዓመት፡ ወበሙጻኡ፡ ወበትእዛዙ፡ በኵሉ፡ ወርኅ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ሰንበት።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: He showed me all their order: for each day, for every period of rule, for every year, and its going out and its command for every month and every week.[a]

footnotes.text: The source changes from I-have-shown-you in79:1 to he-showed-me here; that shift is retained. The closing going-out and command have singular possessive endings, retained as its rather than silently harmonized to their. Period renders the broad time word ዘመን; the source separately says year, month and Sabbath/week. No particular modern orbital or calendar system is supplied.

source.text: ወሐጸጸ፡ ወርኅ፡ ዘ*ይትገበር፡ በ*ሳድስት፡ ኆኅት፡ እስመ፡ በዛቲ፡ ኆኅት፡ ሳድስት፡ ይትፌጸም፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ወ*እምኔሁ፡ ይከውን፡ ርእሰ፡ ታሕጻጼት።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: The waning of the moon takes place in the sixth gate, for in this sixth gate its light reaches fullness, and from there the waning begins.[a]

footnotes.text: Dillmann1865 col136 explicitly cites79:3 under the noun for decrease or waning of the moon, and col137 cites79:4 under the related waning noun. The selected sixth gate is retained twice; it is not recalculated or replaced from a modern lunar model. From there construes the selected masculine suffix as referring to the gate just named.

source.text: (ወታሕጻጼት፡) ዘይትገበር፡ በኆኅት፡ ቀዳሚት፡ በዘመኑ፡ ዚአሁ፡ እስከ፡ ይትፌጸም፡ መዋዕል፡ ፻ወ፸ወ፯፡ በሥርዓተ፡ ሰንበት፡ *፳ወ፭፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ መዋዕል።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification. Actual numerical forms ፻ወ፸ወ፯ and *፳ወ፭ and spelled-out ክልኤቱ preserved; Latin apparatus51/54/56 are not scripture numerals.

translation.text: The waning that takes place in the first gate, in its own period, continues until 177 days are completed: 25 weeks and two days.[a]

footnotes.text: The opening and-the-waning is enclosed in parentheses in the actual edition. Charles printed151 note51 says it was lost through a same-ending omission and supplied here; it is an editor restoration, not an independently observed manuscript reading. The running text prints177 and25 in Ethiopic numerals but writes two as a word. The arithmetic25×7+2=177 is a consistency check, not permission to normalize any other printed number. Continues supplies the elliptical English predicate rather than adding new Geʽez.

source.text: የኀጽጹ፡ እምፀሐይ፡ ወበሥርዓተ፡ ከዋክብት፡ ኀሙሰ፡ መዋዕለ፡ በ*ዘመን፡ አሐዱ፡ ጥንቁቀ፡ ወሶበ፡ ይትፈጸም፡ *ዘመካን፡ ዘትሬኢ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: They fall short of the sun—and of the order of the stars—by five days in one exact period; and when the place you see is completed…[a]

footnotes.text: The plural they is not replaced by a silently identified moon or half-year. The selected prepositional construction is difficult: Charles printed152 note2 discusses an emended preposition understood as from in an enumeration and identifies solar and sidereal years; those are his editorial explanation, not modern calculations added here. The final and-when clause ends the actual numbered unit and is syntactically suspended. The English ellipsis marks that suspension, not an omitted photographed continuation. Place renders selected መካን without specifying a modern astronomical station. This candidate does not claim the clause is fully reconstructed.

source.text: ከመዝ፡ አርአያ፡ ወእምሳል፡ እምኵሉ፡ ብርሃን፡ ዘአርአየኒ፡ ኡርኤል፡ መልአክ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ መራኂሆሙ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: Such is the appearance and pattern of all the light that Uriel, the great angel who is their leader, showed me.

source.text: ወበውእቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ኡርኤል፡ መልአክ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ነዋ፡ አርአይኩከ፡ ኵሎ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ወኵሎ፡ ከሠትኩ፡ ለከ፡ ትርአዮ፡ ለዝ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወለዝ፡ ወርኅ፡ ወለእለ፡ ይመርኅዎሙ፡ ለ*ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወለ*ኵሎሙ፡ እለ፡ ይመይጥዎሙ፡ ግብሮሙ፡ ወአዝማኖሙ፡ ወ*ሙባኢሆሙ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: In those days the angel Uriel answered me and said, “Look, Enoch, I have shown you everything and revealed it all to you, so that you may see this sun and this moon, those who lead the stars of heaven, and all who turn them—their activities, their periods, and their entrances.[a]”

footnotes.text: The selected ending is compressed: all who turn them is followed by their activities, periods and entrances. This English keeps the turning verb and the plural possessives instead of silently replacing the agents with modern orbital forces. Entrances renders the noun of coming in, not a supplied named point of setting or rising.

source.text: ወ*በመዋዕለ፡ ኃጥኣን፡ ክረማት፡ የኀጽሩ፡ ወ*ዘርአ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ይከውን፡ ዳኃራዊ፡ በምድረሙ፡ ወበወፍሮሙ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ግብር፡ ዘዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ይትመየጥ፡ ወኢያስተርኢ፡ ለአዝማኖሙ፡ ወዝናም፡ ይትከላእ፡ ወሰማይ፡ ታቀውም።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification. One actual star before በመዋዕለ; raised21 does not create a second star. No star printed before ምድረሙ or አዝማኖሙ: raised26 after በ and31 after ለ are apparatus numbers.

translation.text: “In the days of sinners the years will grow shorter. Their crops will be late on their land and in their fields. Everything done upon the earth will change and will not appear at its proper times. Rain will be withheld, and the sky will hold it back.[a]”

footnotes.text: Dillmann1865 col834 gives year as a sense of ክረምት and explicitly cites80:2; col623 supports the intransitive shortening verb, and col949 gives selected ወፍር as fields or cultivated land. The final verb is the causative stopping/holding-back form, not simply the sky will stand. Col453 gives restrain/hold back and explicitly cites80:2 in its related delaying range; it, referring to the just-mentioned rain, is supplied in English. The printed negative before appear is retained.

source.text: ወበውእቱ፡ አዝማን፡ ፍሬ፡ ምድር፡ ደሓራዊ፡ ይከውን፡ ወኢይበቍል፡ በዘመኑ፡ ወፍሬ፡ ዕፅ፡ ይትከላእ፡ በዘመኑ፡ ዚአሁ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: “In those times the earth’s produce will be late and will not sprout in its proper season, and the fruit of the trees will be withheld in its own season.”

source.text: ወወርኅ፡ ይዌልጥ፡ ሥርዓቶ፡ ወኢይትረአይ፡ በዘመኑ፡ ዚአሁ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: “The moon will change its order and will not appear at its own time.”

source.text: [ወበእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ይትረአይ፡ †ሰማይ፡ ወይበጽሕ፡ †ዐባር፡ በጽንፈ፡ ሰረገላት፡ ዐቢይ፡ ለምዕራብ፡] ወይበርህ፡ ፈድፋደ፡ እምሥርዓተ፡ ብርሃን።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification. Full opening [ ] span retained and both initial dagger signs; no sun/evening emendation inserted into the selected source.

translation.text: “[In those days the sky will appear and reach drought at the edge of the great chariot toward the west.][a] It will shine beyond the prescribed order of light.”

footnotes.text: The bracketed clause is not sound, assured narrative. The edition daggers sky and drought/famine and brackets the entire opening as an interpolation (Charles printed153 notes1–4). Dillmann1865 col984 explicitly cites80:5 for drought, scarcity or famine; cols347–348 support chariot/wheel, not a supplied modern constellation. Charles reports a conjectural explanation involving Hebrew sun versus sky and evening versus hunger; those conjectures are not independently examined manuscript readings and are not silently substituted in this diplomatic English. The difficult reach-drought expression remains unresolved. The source retains two initial daggers as actually printed, not invented paired closing signs.

source.text: ወይሥሕቱ፡ ብዙኃን፡ አርእስቲሆሙ፡ ለ*ከዋክብት፡ ትእዛዘ፡ ወእሉ፡ ይመይጡ፡ ፍናዊሆሙ፡ ወግብሮሙ፡ ወኢይትረአዩ፡ በአዝማነ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ እለ፡ ተአዘዙ፡ ሎሙ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification. Actual በአዝማነ checked on enlarged source image; raw OCR በዘዝማነ rejected, no later text supplies the correction.

translation.text: “Many of the heads of the stars will stray from the command. These will change their paths and their activities, and they will not appear at the times appointed for them.”

source.text: ወኵሉ፡ ሥርዓተ፡ ከዋክብት፡ ይትዐፀው፡ ላዕለ፡ ኃጥኣን፡ ወሕሊናሆሙ፡ ለእለ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ይስሕቱ፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ [ወይትመየጡ፡ እምኵሉ፡ ፍናዋቲሆሙ፡] ወይስሕቱ፡ ወይመስልዎሙ፡ አማልክተ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: “The whole order of the stars will be shut off from sinners. The thoughts of those on earth will go astray concerning them. [They will turn away from all their paths.][a] They will go astray and consider them gods.”

footnotes.text: The clause they-will-turn-away-from-all-their-paths is bracketed in the selected edition. Charles printed153 note20 calls it an interpolation and explains the difficulty of attaching it to either people or stars. This English retains it visibly bracketed without deciding that disputed referent. The following consider-them-gods clause is not translated as genuine divine status. Dillmann1865 col1022 explicitly cites80:7 for the shut-off construction with the preposition used here.

source.text: ወይበዝኅ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ፡ እኩይ፡ ወመቅሠፍት፡ ይመጽእ፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ ከመ፡ ታሕጕል፡ ኵሎ።
source.note: Direct selected Charles1906 actual primary-photo collation, printed151–153/PDF189–191. Actual critical asterisks, daggers, square brackets and editor-supplied parentheses retained. Raised apparatus references removed; numerical text is not inferred from modern astronomy. Punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English source or independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: “Evil will increase upon them, and a scourge will come upon them so as to destroy everything.”
